name: Dependencies

require.label: lock at least one dependency in the manifest

blurb: Lock the libraries every repo depends on — once, so the fleet never fights over them.
prompt:
Lock the project's dependencies ONCE, here, so the parallel fleet never each adds and redefines
them in their own worktrees (which collide at integration). Knowing the stack, the linked repos, and
the features, enumerate the libraries each repo needs.

Write them to `dependencies.json` — a JSON array, one entry per library:
```json
[
  { "repo": "owner/app", "ecosystem": "npm",   "name": "zod",   "version": "^3.23", "why": "runtime schema validation" },
  { "repo": "owner/app", "ecosystem": "npm",   "name": "vitest", "version": "^2.0",  "dev": true, "why": "unit tests" },
  { "repo": "owner/api", "ecosystem": "cargo", "name": "serde",  "version": "1",      "why": "(de)serialization" }
]
```
Fields: `repo` (`owner/repo`; omit to apply to every repo of that ecosystem), `ecosystem` (`npm` or
`cargo`), `name`, `version` (a range/version; omit ⇒ latest), `dev` (true for dev/test-only deps),
and a one-line `why`. Propose the set, interrogate it (is each one needed? right version? runtime vs
dev?), then write the file. These become each repo's real `package.json` / `Cargo.toml` at publish and
are inlined into every worker as the locked, authoritative set.

Gate: at least one dependency is locked in `dependencies.json`.
